solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Theatrical and exaggerated Frenchman in beret

indicators.note: in tells us the Frenchman's letter sits inside the headgear

parts.note: a beret is a kind of cap
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: An over-the-top Frenchman sporting a beret, like a stage caricature.
explanation.walkthrough: M is short for Monsieur, the French form of Mr.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes deliberately showy, affected, theatrical behaviour or style.

clue.text: Familiar with monarch but no aristocrat

parts.note: common means ordinary or familiar
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone close to the monarch who has no noble title.
explanation.definitionFit: A commoner is a person without a title, someone outside the nobility.

clue.text: Chop rotten at one end consumed by rodents

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up, so the picked letter sits inside the rodents

parts.note: mice are small rodents

indicators.note: at one end picks a letter from an extremity of the word, here its final letter

explanation.surface: Mice eating something rotten, chopped up at one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince food is to chop it very finely.

clue.text: Bond chasing chess player in formal attire

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the tie follows the chess player in the answer

parts.note: Black is one of the two players in a game of chess
a tie is something that binds, a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond pursuing a chess opponent while dressed in a dinner suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007 rather than a plain synonym for a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tie is the dress code for dinner jackets and evening gowns, i.e. formal clothing.

clue.text: Pretentious boy on Cretan mountain

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Mount Ida is the highest peak on Crete

explanation.surface: A conceited boy perched on a mountain in Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes affected, snobbish manners or speech.

clue.text: Vanishing cream consumer?

parts.note: vanishing cream is a cosmetic, but read as a vanishing cream-drinker it is the cat in Alice in Wonderland that fades away

explanation.surface: A user of a skin cream that disappears into the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's grinning cat vanishes until only its smile remains; cats famously lap cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alice character disappears at will, and as a cat it would drink cream.

clue.text: Rate revised within the playhouse

indicators.note: revised means altered, so these four letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Ticket prices changed inside the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' suggests a container but here only joins the pieces; 'revised' gives ATRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a building where plays are staged.

clue.text: Takes in tea brewed by son

indicators.note: brewed suggests the letters are stewed together into a new order

explanation.surface: A son making tea and drinking it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in food is to eat it, consume it.

clue.text: Exotic mink and sentient apes

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so these letters are rearranged into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A zoo-like list of an unusual mink and some intelligent primates.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans are thinking great apes, so the human race can be wryly described this way.

clue.text: Wise men in island country offering vision

indicators.note: in places the wise men within the island-plus-country letters

parts.note: a nation is a country
the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity

explanation.surface: The Three Wise Men arriving in an island nation, bringing a vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision in the sense of creative foresight is imagination.

clue.text: Still time for adventure

parts.note: still can mean even, as in 'even better' / 'still better'

explanation.surface: There is still time left for an adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb of time but gives EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a notable happening, which is one sense of an event.

clue.text: What doors should do is obvious

definitions.meaning: an ... case is one that is plainly clear-cut

explanation.surface: Stating that a door's purpose is self-evident.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut matter is straightforward, easily decided, with no doubt about it.

clue.text: Swinger has choice about complete uniform

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the choice wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a plum is the best or choicest thing, as in a plum job
to end something is to complete it
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man-about-town picks his outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' hints at a party-goer but means something that swings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is a weight that swings to and fro, as in a clock.

clue.text: Potion team in anger knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means sent back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
in places the team inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A potion that an angry team downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking the potion, but it reverses RI(XI)LE. 'Anger' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical or medicinal drink, a kind of potion.

clue.text: Sloth one near it disturbed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone lazily lying near it is roused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' suggests the animal, but means idleness. 'Disturbed' rearranges NEAR IT to NERTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, a reluctance to move, which inertia also denotes.

clue.text: Picnic in light wind

definitions.meaning: a picnic informally means something easy

explanation.surface: Eating outdoors in a gentle wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'no picnic' and 'a breeze' describe how easy a task is; a breeze is also a mild wind.

clue.text: Hot stone cracked around lake

indicators.note: around says the reshuffled letters wrap round the lake's letter
cracked means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sun-heated stone split open beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' rearranges STONE to STOEN, which goes around L. 'Hot' is slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot goods, in criminal slang, are recently taken goods that are risky to sell.

clue.text: Office item most recent one used in City group

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so these pieces go within the City's letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
last means most recent, as in 'last week'
I is the Roman numeral one
a band is a group, musical or otherwise

explanation.surface: A stationery item recently used by a band from the City.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London, its financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber bands of this kind are standard stationery found on desks.

clue.text: Parched swallowing cold bitter

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the cold letter goes within the dry word

parts.note: arid means parched, dry

explanation.surface: A thirsty person gulping down a cold, bitter drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like a pub beer, the English pale ale, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid taste or smell is sharp and unpleasantly bitter.

clue.text: Love shown by husband leaving this regretful lady

parts.note: O, a zero score in tennis, is love

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the husband's letter is taken out of the word

explanation.surface: A woman sorry that her husband has walked out on her love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Otis Regrets' is a Cole Porter song in which Miss Otis apologises she cannot lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Cole Porter song expresses regret, so she is a lady who regrets.

clue.text: Rwandan king of old is back

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, was an ancient Egyptian king

indicators.note: back means the short word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A former Rwandan monarch has returned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi, so a Tutsi is a Rwandan.

clue.text: Bananas all tear on the side

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Bananas torn apart along their sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit but is the crazy-signal for ALL TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to or situated at the side.

clue.text: Good bread in fact stale

indicators.note: in puts the good bread inside the fact

parts.note: a stat, short for statistic, is a fact
naan or nan is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: Good bread that is, in fact, stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' reads as a filler phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and a stat (statistic) is a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water or ideas have gone stale and lifeless from lack of movement.

clue.text: Cheese some sent back from a delicatessen

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some cheese returned to the deli it came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks MADE from 'from a delicatessen'; 'sent back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese sold in red-waxed balls.
